name: "Forania" indet.
basis: Forania is a zosterophyll with branched, spinose axes and lateral bivalved sporangia.
source: [Jensen & Gensel (2013), Forania plegiospinosa: A Zosterophyll from the Early Devonian](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/pdfplus/10.1086/669914), abstract.

name: <"Kaulangiophyton">
basis: Kaulangiophyton comprises branched shoots bearing sporangia and is assigned to the zosterophyll lineage.
source: [USGS, Index of Generic Names of Fossil Plants, 1966–1973, Kaulangiophyton entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1396/report.pdf), indexed passage.

name: <"Leclercqia">
basis: Leclercqia is a microphyllous lycopsid; ligules are documented in its type species.
source: [Grierson & Bonamo (1979), Leclercqia complexa: Earliest Ligulate Lycopod](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1979.tb06248.x).

name: <"Leclerqia">
basis: Interpreted as a misspelling of Leclercqia, the ligulate lycopsid, rather than a distinct genus.
source: [Grierson & Bonamo (1979), Leclercqia complexa: Earliest Ligulate Lycopod](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1979.tb06248.x).

name: <Articulale>
basis: The extract records a sterile axis; the informal label does not establish articulated sphenopsid morphology or vascular anatomy.
source: none checked

name: <Lycopsids>
basis: The identification explicitly denotes lycopsids; these flags classify that named group, conditional on the sterile-axis identification.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: <Morphotype I>
basis: An anonymous sterile-axis morphotype supplies no diagnostic reproductive or anatomical evidence for a vascular lineage.
source: none checked

name: <Morphotype II>
basis: The sterile-axis record and anonymous morphotype label do not establish sporangia, tracheids or a particular land-plant lineage.
source: none checked

name: <Morphotype III>
basis: Published material assigned to Tanner's morphotype III consists of axes radiating from a common attachment; diagnostic fertility and vascular anatomy remain unestablished.
source: [Caruso & Tomescu (2012), Microconchid encrusters colonizing land plants](https://mihaibotany.online/pdf/Caruso%202012%20Lethaia.pdf), text and figure 1F–G.

name: <Trimerophyte>
basis: Trimerophytes are basal euphyllophytes. This classifies the informal group identification without independently validating the occurrence.
source: [Cantino et al. (2007), Towards a phylogenetic nomenclature of Tracheophyta](https://donoghuelab.yale.edu/sites/default/files/165_cantino_taxon07.pdf), discussion of Pan-Euphyllophyta.

name: <zosterophylloid>
basis: The label denotes a zosterophyll; the Canadian zosterophylloid-axis material was subsequently associated with Bathurstia denticulata.
source: [Kotyk (1998), Late Silurian and Early Devonian fossil plants of Bathurst Island](https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstreams/518d9179-7afe-4dd9-88b1-1833d37449e8/download), indexed primary-text passages.

name: ? Euomphalopteris sp.
basis: Euomphalopteris is a marine gastropod name appearing in the original Alaskan faunal list. This is non-plant contamination of the extract, rather than an anomalously aged land plant.
source: [USGS Professional Paper 87, Geology of the Hanagita–Bremner Region and southeastern Alaska contributions](https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0087/report.pdf), Kasaan Peninsula faunal list, p. 71, indexed passage.

name: ? Pachytheca sp.
basis: Pachytheca comprises small spheres with differentiated filamentous tissues and conjectural, commonly algal affinities; it is not an accepted embryophyte.
source: [Gerrienne, Les Pachytheca de La Gileppe et de Nonceveux](https://popups.ulg.ac.be/0037-9395/index.php?id=1298&lang=en), published abstract.

name: ? Protaxites loganii
basis: Interpreted as a misspelling of Prototaxites loganii, a tubular, non-vascular problematic organism rather than a branched embryophyte sporophyte.
source: [Retallack & Landing (2014), Affinities and architecture of Devonian trunks of Prototaxites loganii](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24990121/), abstract.

name: ? Protoarticulata indet.
basis: Høeg's material consists of axes with irregular verticils and possible leaf bases, explicitly retained incertae sedis despite comparison with Hyenia.
source: [Høeg (1942), The Downtonian and Devonian flora of Spitsbergen](https://brage.npolar.no/npolar-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/173926/Skrifter083.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), p. 88, indexed passage.

name: ? Psilophyte indet.
basis: The historical specimen is a slender axis with two isotomous bifurcations, subsequently compared with Hostinella; diagnostic fertility is lacking.
source: [Prestianni et al. (2012), Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 179:44–55](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/137700/1/Prestiannietal2012.pdf), section 5.5.2.

name: Aarabia brevicaulis n. gen. n. sp.
basis: Pseudomonopodial shoots bear differentiated lateral branching systems and elongate terminal sporangia; the published analysis associates Aarabia with basal euphyllophytes.
source: [Meyer-Berthaud & Gerrienne (2001), Aarabia, a new Early Devonian vascular plant from Africa](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S003466670100063X), abstract and conclusion.

name: Aberlemnia sp.
basis: Aberlemnia has dichotomous axes with terminal, bivalved sporangia and is interpreted as a basal member of Lycophytina.
source: [Libertín, Kvaček & Bek (2024), The genus Aberlemnia and its Silurian–Devonian fossil record](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034666723001860), abstract and highlights.

name: Actinophyllum
basis: The historical fossil was compared with an alga, but the consulted geological account retains uncertain affinity; secure embryophyte characters are not established.
source: [Cleal & Thomas, Palaeozoic Palaeobotany of Great Britain, Silurian chapter](https://data.jncc.gov.uk/data/a2ed7572-87e2-40b9-93cf-2f3af82d8797/gcr-v9-palaeozoic-palaeobotany-of-great-britain-c3.pdf), Actinophyllum discussion.

name: Actinopodium nathorstii
basis: Permineralised axes have a stellate vascular system and secondary xylem; Actinopodium is included among archaeopteridalean progymnosperms.
source: [Cornet et al. (2012), A Middle Devonian Callixylon from Ronquières, Belgium](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/129376/1/Cornet%20et%20al.,%202012..pdf), introduction.

name: Anaeurophyton germanicum
basis: Interpreted as a spelling error for Aneurophyton germanicum, an aneurophytalean progymnosperm with complex branching systems and woody axes.
source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm, Bavarian State Collection](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

name: Anapaulia moodyi
basis: Whorled branching systems and dichotomising appendages support the published interpretation as a probable iridopteridalean.
source: [Berry & Edwards (1996), Anapaulia moodyi: a probable iridopteridalean compression fossil](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10072/), abstract.

name: Aneurophytales
basis: Aneurophytales are woody, spore-producing progymnosperms on the euphyllophyte lineage.
source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

name: Aneurophyton germanicum
basis: Aneurophyton germanicum is an aneurophytalean progymnosperm with spirally arranged, repeatedly divided branching systems.
source: [Krings (2024), Branch system of a progymnosperm](https://bspg.snsb.de/oktober-2024-xxx/?lang=en).

name: Aneurophyton hallii
basis: Material historically assigned this name includes the woody aneurophytalean subsequently revised as Triloboxylon arnoldii; species-level synonymy requires care.
source: [Stein & Beck (1983), Triloboxylon arnoldii from the Middle Devonian of Western New York](https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/48520/2/ID372.pdf), indexed abstract and synonymy.

name: Angarolaminariopsis zinovae
basis: The consulted account records its provisional assignment to Laminariales; this supports an algal interpretation without establishing that it was a true kelp.
source: [Zerov (1972), Essay on the phylogeny of non-vascular plants](https://ru.djvu.online/file/HkY3t7gfb3lE0), indexed digitised text discussing Ananiev's material.

name: Anisophyton cf. gothanii
basis: Anisophyton is placed within the sawdoniaceous zosterophylls; the species comparison remains provisional.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/), phylogeny and illustrated Anisophyton material.

name: Aphyllopteris
basis: Aphyllopteris is a form-genus for incomplete leafless branching axes; its architecture alone does not establish a particular vascular lineage.
source: [Høeg (1952), Psilophytites, a new form genus of Devonian plants](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.54991/jop.1952.409), indexed discussion of Aphyllopteris.

name: Archaeosigillaria
basis: Archaeosigillaria is a lycopsid genus, although revision has reassigned some historically included species.
source: [Berry & Edwards (1997), A new species of Gilboaphyton, with a revision of Archaeosigillaria](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034666796000152).

name: Asterocalamites
basis: This archaeocalamitalean sphenopsid has a documented range beginning in the Late Devonian; the Pragian identification requires correction.
source: [Newfoundland Geological Survey, Current Research (1999), Boyce contribution](https://www.gov.nl.ca/em/files/mines-geoscience-publications-currentresearch-1999-boyce.pdf), indexed Asterocalamites/Archaeocalamites discussion.

name: Asteroxylon
basis: Anatomically demonstrated drepanophycalean lycopsid with leafy shoots and differentiated rooting systems.
source: [Hetherington et al. (2021), Asteroxylon reconstruction and rooting-system study](https://elifesciences.org/articles/69447).

name: Baragwanathia
basis: Microphyllous shoots and vascular anatomy establish lycopsid affinity; disputed earliest occurrence ages do not alter this placement.
source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf), Baragwanathia discussion.

name: Baragwanathia longifolia
basis: Its microphyllous morphology and anatomy support lycopsid placement; the debated dating of particular Australian records is a separate issue.
source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf).

name: Baragwanthia longifolia
basis: The Australian context identifies this as a spelling variant of Baragwanathia longifolia, a microphyllous lycopsid.
source: [Selden & Edwards, Colonisation of the land](https://www.paulselden.net/uploads/7/5/3/2/7532217/colonisation.pdf).

name: Barinophyton
basis: Recent phylogenetic analyses place barinophytes within Lycophytina, among the zosterophyll grade.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Barsassia ornata
basis: Modern revision identifies a herbaceous lycopsid with imbricate leaves and vascular anatomy, superseding the legacy psilophyte grouping.
source: [Liu et al. (2021), Barsassia morphology and nomenclatural revision](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703484/).

name: Bathurstia cf. denticulata
basis: Bathurstia is a zosterophyll within Lycophytina; the species identification is explicitly tentative.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Bathurstia denticulata n. gen. n. sp.
basis: Bathurstia is recovered within Lycophytina, close to the barinophytes.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Bathurstia sp.
basis: The genus denotes a zosterophyll; its identification from this axis remains conditional.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Bergeria
basis: The identified B. mimerensis material consists of lepidophytic stems with leaf cushions; its precise relationship to other Devonian lycopsids remains unresolved.
source: [Høeg (1942), The Downtonian and Devonian flora of Spitsbergen](https://brage.npolar.no/npolar-xmlui/bitstream/handle/11250/173926/Skrifter083.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), original-description excerpts.

name: Bitelaria dubjanskii
basis: Canadian material was reinterpreted as a vascular land plant rather than an alga, but its position relative to the lycophyte–euphyllophyte split remains unresolved.
source: [Johnson & Gensel (1992), Bitelaria study](https://eurekamag.com/research/008/071/008071253.php); [published abstract reproduced](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/018/452/018452481.php).

name: Blasaria
basis: Blasaria was founded on lycopod leaf-base impressions; the named genus supports lycophyte affinity, with incomplete evidence for every included species.
source: [USGS generic index, Blasaria entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1013/report.pdf); [Liu et al. (2021), comparison with Barsassia](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703484/).

name: Bowerophylloides mendozaensis
basis: The original account describes sterile leafy axes that cannot be unequivocally assigned to established taxa; reproductive and diagnostic vascular characters are lacking.
source: [Edwards et al. (2001), Bowerophylloides original account](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10065/), abstract.

name: Caia langii n. gen. n. sp.
basis: Dichotomous naked axes terminate in elongate sporangia containing trilete spores; comparison with Horneophyton supports rhyniophytoid organisation.
source: [Fanning et al. (1990), Caia original description](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10177/), abstract.

name: Calamophyton
basis: Calamophyton is a pseudosporochnalean cladoxylopsid reconstructed from connected trunks, branching crowns and roots.
source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton whole-plant reconstruction](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/), abstract.

name: Calamophyton primaevum
basis: This genuine Middle Devonian species is a cladoxylopsid with organically connected trunk, crown and rooting structures.
source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton whole-plant reconstruction](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/).

name: Callixylon
basis: Callixylon denotes archaeopteridalean progymnosperm wood, characterised by grouped tracheid pitting. PBDB's cordaitalean placement is inappropriate.
source: [Cornet et al. (2012), A Middle Devonian Callixylon from Ronquières, Belgium](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/129376/1/Cornet%20et%20al.,%202012..pdf).

name: Catenalis digitata
basis: The original account describes branched axes with putative sporangia but cannot establish typical tracheids and entertains both algal and vascular-plant interpretations.
source: [Hao & Beck (1991), Catenalis digitata](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237164533_Catenalis_digitata_gen_et_spnov_a_plant_from_the_Lower_Devonian_Siegenian_of_Yunnan_China), reproduced abstract.

name: Caulopteris
basis: The identified Devonian species were described as fern-like stems with petiole or leaf-scar characters; broad euphyllophyte affinity is more defensible than a specific marattialean assignment.
source: [Dawson (1888), The Geological History of Plants](https://readingroo.ms/5/1/0/2/51021/51021-h/51021-h.htm), descriptions of Devonian Caulopteris.

name: Cephalopteris
basis: The actual identification is C. praecox, subsequently Protocephalopteris praecox, a Devonian fern-like plant; it should not inherit the old genus's seed-fern assignment.
source: [Xue & Basinger (2016), Melvillipteris quadriseriata](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283145584_Melvillipteris_quadriseriata_gen_et_sp_nov_a_new_plant_from_the_Upper_Devonian_Famennian_of_Arctic_Canada), published comparison.

name: Chaleuria cirrosa
basis: Monopodial axes bear dichotomous ultimate branches and paired terminal sporangia; the original authors suggested primitive progymnosperm affinities.
source: [Andrews, Gensel & Forbes (1974), An apparently heterosporous plant from the Middle Devonian of New Brunswick](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_17/vol17_part2_pp387-408.pdf).

name: Chauvinia scharyana
basis: This historical fossil name denotes Protolepidodendron scharianum material with lepidodendroid shoots and narrow, sometimes divided leaves, rather than the living algal homonym.
source: [USGS generic index, Chauvinia entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf); [Jahn (1903), description and synonymy](https://opac.geologie.ac.at/ais312/dokumente/Verh_kk_geol_RA_1903_komplett.pdf), indexed passages.

name: Ciguelia juvenile n. gen. n. sp.
basis: The original abstract groups Ciguelia among sterile, simply dichotomising axes; diagnostic fertility and vascular anatomy are not established in the consulted material.
source: [Mussa et al. (1996), original abstract reproduced on this literature page](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326217684_EARLY_DEVONIAN_TAPHOFLORA_RECORD_IN_PONTA_GROSSA_ARCH_PARANA_BASIN_SOUTHERN_BRAZIL_AND_ITS_PALAEOGEOGRAPHIC_IMPLICATIONS_REGISTRO_DA_TAFOFLORA_DEVONIANA_NO_ARCO_DE_PONTA_GROSSA_BACIA_DO_PARANA_SUL_DO_).

name: Cladophlebis
basis: Cladophlebis is a younger fern-foliage morphogenus, particularly characteristic of Mesozoic floras; the enormous collection-age interval does not establish an early Palaeozoic occurrence.
source: [Jud et al. (2013), discussion of Cladophlebis foliage](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.3732/ajb.1200637).

name: Cladoxylon
basis: The identified C. scoparium is a genuine Devonian cladoxylopsid, associated in modern reconstruction with Calamophyton primaevum.
source: [Giesen & Berry (2013), Calamophyton reconstruction and synonymy](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/47293/).

name: Cladoxylopsida
basis: Cladoxylopsids are euphyllophytes, despite continuing uncertainty over their relationships within that lineage.
source: [Durieux et al. (2026), Systematics and evolution of cladoxylopsids](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-paleontology/article/systematics-and-evolution-of-cladoxylopsids-a-consequential-yet-underappreciated-tracheophyte-group-with-a-deep-fossil-history/BA2D34F54ABDA687AFA0672771F708E5).

name: Coactilum
basis: A calcimicrobe traditionally treated as a schizophyte alga and referred to Rothpletzella; precise microbial affinity is uncertain, but embryophyte affinity is unsupported.
source: [Liu et al. (2016), Tarim calcimicrobe systematic account](https://robertriding.com/pdf/liu-etal-2016-tarim.pdf).

name: Codonophycus austinii
basis: The taxon is an alga described from the Mississippian Madison Formation; the broad PBDB interval supplies no evidence of a Devonian occurrence.
source: [USGS generic index, Codonophycus entry, p. 56](https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark%3A/67531/metadc1114957/m1/62/), indexed entry.

name: Colpodexylon
basis: A protolepidodendralean lycopsid with characteristically divided microphylls.
source: [Edwards & Benedetto (1985), Devonian lycophyte systematic account](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_28/vol28_part3_pp599-618.pdf).

name: Colpodexylon deatsii
basis: The lycopsid type species has lobed xylem and trifurcate leaves. Its Frasnian type record warrants checking this particular Middle Devonian identification.
source: [Edwards & Benedetto (1985)](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_28/vol28_part3_pp599-618.pdf), Colpodexylon comparison.

name: Compsocradus laevigatus
basis: An anatomically documented iridopteridalean with a six-ribbed mesarch vascular system and complex lateral branching.
source: [Berry & Stein (2000), Compsocradus laevigatus](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/314295), abstract.

name: Conchulophyton quadrosii n. gen. n. sp.
basis: Bibliographic metadata confirms the name, but no diagnostic description was recovered; its Furnas provenance alone cannot establish biological affinity.
source: [Mussa et al. (2002), New taxa from the Furnas Formation: institutional catalogue](https://www.infraestruturameioambiente.sp.gov.br/institutodebotanica/2002/01/new-taxa-from-the-furnas-formation-parana-basin-brasil-an-approach-and-revalidation-of-names/), metadata only.

name: Cooksonia
basis: Branched sporophytes bear terminal sporangia; heterogeneous historical usage and unresolved phylogenetic placement prevent a secure crown-tracheophyte assignment.
source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

name: Cooksonia hemisphaerica
basis: Branched axes terminate in hemispherical sporangia; poor preservation leaves its precise systematic position unresolved.
source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

name: Cooksonia pertoni
basis: Tracheids establish vascular status, but published phylogenetic analyses do not securely settle placement relative to the crown-tracheophyte node.
source: Gonez & Gerrienne (2010), A new definition and a lectotypification of the genus Cooksonia Lang 1937, International Journal of Plant Sciences 171:199–215; full local PDF consulted.

name: Crenaticaulis
basis: A sawdoniaceous zosterophyll within Lycophytina.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Cryptoxylon forfarense
basis: Kidston and Lang transferred this fossil to Nematophyton; its pseudoparenchymatous organisation does not represent vascular wood.
source: [Kidston & Lang (1924), Notes on fossil plants from the Old Red Sandstone of Scotland: Nematophyton forfarense](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/earth-and-environmental-science-transactions-of-royal-society-of-edinburgh/article/abs/xxixnotes-on-fossil-plants-from-the-old-red-sandstone-of-scotland-ii-nematophyton-forfarense-kidston-sp-iii-on-two-species-of-pachytheca-p-media-and-p-fasciculata-based-on-the-characters-of-the-algal-filaments/70862AE7D7A9C1D5A6F6B08DB13A7D7F), extract.

name: Dadoxylon
basis: The identified D. cf. halli denotes secondary wood consistent with a lignophyte; its precise whole-plant association remains unproved.
source: [Knowlton, Revision of Araucarioxylon](https://repository.si.edu/bitstreams/66b52b0c-1ca2-460b-a6b4-f8c86a6da839/download), discussion of Dadoxylon halli.

name: Dalejophyton nemejci
basis: A later assessment interprets the supposed sporangia as probably unflattened coiled sterile tips; anatomy and epidermal characters remain unknown.
source: [Broushkin & Gordenko, Istchenkophyton filiciforme](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225638287_Istchenkophyton_filiciforme_gen_et_sp_nov_a_New_Small_Vascular_Plant_with_Thick_Cuticle_from_the_Devonian_of_Voronezh_Region_European_Russia), published comparison excerpt.

name: Dawsonites
basis: A form-genus for isolated fertile branching systems resembling Psilophyton and other basal euphyllophytes, rather than a securely reconstructed natural genus.
source: [Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf), Dawsonites discussion.

name: Dawsonites arcuatus
basis: Clusters of pendulous fusiform sporangia are interpreted as trimerophyte fertile organs; some better-characterised material has been reassigned to Psilophyton.
source: [Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf).

name: Distichophytum
basis: A zosterophyll recovered within Lycophytina in recent analyses.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Drepanophycus
basis: A microphyllous lycopsid, despite its legacy PBDB psilophyte grouping.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/).

name: Drepanophycus gaspianus
basis: A microphyllous lycophyte; predominantly vegetative material and poorly known fertility complicate discrimination from related genera.
source: [Li & Edwards (1997), published abstract](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21708551/); [Kotyk (1998), Bathurst Island fossil plants](https://harvest.usask.ca/bitstream/handle/10388/12414/Kotyk_Michelle_Elizabeth_Ann_1998_sec.pdf?isAllowed=y&sequence=1), pp. 63–64.

name: Drepanophycus spinaeformis
basis: An anatomically documented lycophyte with protostelic xylem and annular or helical tracheids.
source: [The effect of pyrite on the tracheid structure of Drepanophycus spinaeformis (1981)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666781900063), abstract.

name: Dutoitea
basis: The actual identification, D. maraisia, concerns Famennian material; modern revision rejects its rhyniophytoid attribution and compares its fertile appendages with Flabellopteris.
source: [Gess & Prestianni, Flabellopteris lococannensis](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302493/1/1-s2.0-S0034666721002098-main.pdf), section 7.

name: Dutoitia
basis: The identified D. alfreda was described as a branched plant with terminal sporangia, but its relationship to the rhyniophytoid type species and vascular lineages remains uncertain.
source: [Plumstead (1967), original description of Dutoitia alfreda](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/bitstreams/9fdfc1a6-f6a5-4295-b5a8-da67d61127d0/download), indexed text and [plate I](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/bitstreams/938bc525-ad4f-4760-a2b2-ed82d61657d5/download).

name: Dutoitia pulchra
basis: The type species has rhyniophytoid organisation; modern reassessment places its locality in the probably Lochkovian Baviaanskloof Formation, contrary to the extract's broad younger interval.
source: [Gess & Prestianni (2021), An early Devonian flora from the Baviaanskloof Formation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8178408/).

name: Enigmophyton
basis: A large fan-leaved vascular-plant morphotype of unresolved affinity; associated reproductive organs should not be transferred to it without organic connection.
source: [Svalbard plants and sediments study (2021)](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/140269/1/JGS%20Accepted%20Svalbard%20Plants%20and%20Sediments%202021.pdf), table 2; [Bateman & DiMichele (1994)](https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/7107/paleo_1994_BatemanDiMichele_Heterospory_BiolRev_small.pdf), p. 381.

name: Enigmophyton superbum
basis: The foliage plant's precise affinity is unresolved; supposedly associated heterosporous fructifications lack organic connection and may belong to Barinophyton.
source: [Bateman & DiMichele (1994), Heterospory: the most iterative key innovation in the evolutionary history of the plant kingdom](https://repository.si.edu/bitstream/handle/10088/7107/paleo_1994_BatemanDiMichele_Heterospory_BiolRev_small.pdf), p. 381.

name: Eocooksonia
basis: Revised material has branching systems terminating in sporangia with triangular emergences; this supports rhyniophytoid organisation rather than unquestioned inheritance of PBDB's zosterophyll placement.
source: [Xue et al. (2015), New observations of the early land plant Eocooksonia from the Pridoli of Xinjiang](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jseaes.2015.02.003), abstract consulted through the Peking University institutional index.

name: Eohostimella heathana
basis: Spinose, dichotomously branching tubular compressions lack known reproductive organs and diagnostic vascular anatomy. Embryophyte identity remains unproved.
source: [Schopf et al. (1966), Erect plants in the early Silurian of Maine](https://pubs.usgs.gov/pp/0550d/report.pdf)

name: Eophyllophyton bellum
basis: Pseudomonopodial branching, divided appendages and terminal sporangial trusses support basal euphyllophyte affinity. Its placement on the euphyllophyte stem still places it within crown Tracheophyta.
source: [Clarke et al. (2011), Establishing a time-scale for plant evolution](https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1469-8137.2011.03794.x)

name: Eorhynia primigenia
basis: Eorhynia has smooth, occasionally dichotomising axes terminated by elongate sporangia. Anatomical preservation does not establish crown-tracheophyte membership.
source: [Edwards and Rogerson (1979), New records of fertile Rhyniophytina from the late Silurian of Wales](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10902/1/Edwards%201979.pdf)

name: Eospermatopteris
basis: Trunks and bases assigned to Eospermatopteris are organically connected to Wattieza crowns, establishing cladoxylopsid affinity.
source: [Stein et al. (2007), Giant cladoxylopsid trees resolve the enigma of the Earth's earliest forest stumps at Gilboa](https://www.nature.com/articles/nature05705)

name: Estinnophyton gracile
basis: Estinnophyton bears divided fertile appendages carrying stalked sporangia and is interpreted as a primitive sphenopsid. The precise sphenopsid relationship is less secure than its broad euphyllophyte affinity.
source: [Hao, Wang and Wang (2004), A new species of Estinnophyton from the Lower Devonian Posongchong Formation, Yunnan, China](https://academic.oup.com/botlinnean/article-abstract/146/2/201/2420369)

name: Euphyllophytina
basis: This higher-group identification denotes the euphyllophyte lineage, sister to Lycophytina within crown vascular plants.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Flabellofolium
basis: Flabellofolium replaces Platyphyllum for isolated, large, fan-shaped leaves. Their parent plants and systematic relationships remain insufficiently resolved for a particular crown lineage.
source: [Snigirevsky and Lyubarova (2023), New fossil plant from the Late Devonian strata of Northern Timan](https://pureportal.spbu.ru/files/116919897/Snigirevsky_Lyubarova_2023.pdf)

name: Foozia minuta
basis: Branched axes bear slender lateral appendages terminating in paired sporangia, with vascular evidence supporting probable cladoxylopsid affinity.
source: [Gerrienne (1992), The Emsian plants from Fooz-Wépion: III. Foozia minuta, a new taxon with probable cladoxylalean affinities](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/101836)

name: Gilboaphyton
basis: Gilboaphyton is a herbaceous lycopsid with diagnostic leaf-base patterns and leaves bearing paired lateral teeth. The PBDB psilophyte grouping is misleading.
source: [Berry and Edwards (1997), A new species of the lycopsid Gilboaphyton from Venezuela and New York State](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0034666796000152)

name: Gosferia curvata
basis: A zosterophyll bearing reniform sporangia on long, abaxially recurved stalks. Gosferia is the replacement name for the preoccupied fossil genus Forgesia.
source: [Gerrienne (1999), Gosferia, a new name for Forgesia](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/271789417_Gosferia_a_new_name_for_Forgesia_fossil_plants)

name: Gosslingia
basis: A zosterophyll genus with branched axes, lateral sporangia and characteristic vascular anatomy.
source: [Edwards (1970), Further observations on the Lower Devonian plant Gosslingia breconensis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22408827/)

name: Gosslingia breconensis
basis: Lateral sporangia, branched axes and anatomically documented xylem establish zosterophyll affinity.
source: [Kenrick and Edwards (1988), The anatomy of Lower Devonian Gosslingia breconensis based on pyritized axes](https://academic.oup.com/botlinnean/article-abstract/97/2/95/2660285)

name: Gumuia zyzzata
basis: Successive lateral and terminal sporangia form a distinctive zigzag fertile system. The original description tentatively assigns the plant to the zosterophylls.
source: [Hao (1989), Gumuia zyzzata, a new plant from the Lower Devonian of Yunnan](https://www.jipb.net/EN/abstract/abstract26800.shtml)

name: Haplostigma
basis: A lycopsid stem morphogenus characterised by regularly arranged appendage bases and surface patterns. The broad affinity is better established than individual species delimitations.
source: [Middle Devonian herbaceous lycopsid Haplostigma from the Paraná Basin (2015)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0016699515000601)

name: Harringtonia
basis: The supplied identification H. acutiplicata matches the Silurian brachiopod Harringtonina acutiplicata. A spelling or name-resolution collision probably explains its placement under cycads.
source: [Carrera et al. (2011), Silurian–Devonian coral associations across a sequence stratigraphic boundary in the Argentine Precordillera](https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/bitstream/handle/11336/24993/CONICET_Digital_Nro.78aff3b5-f870-4e52-81b1-f9ae865fa72f_A.pdf?sequence=2)

name: Haskinsia
basis: A herbaceous lycopsid with dichotomising stems and helically arranged, petiolate leaves. Fertile material documents adaxially attached sporangia.
source: [Berry and Edwards (1996), The herbaceous lycophyte Haskinsia from the Devonian of western Venezuela](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10071/)

name: Haskinsia sagittata
basis: Sagittate leaves and sporangia attached adaxially to otherwise unmodified leaves establish herbaceous lycopsid affinity.
source: [Berry and Edwards (1996), The herbaceous lycophyte Haskinsia from the Devonian of western Venezuela](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10071/)

name: Heidiphyllum
basis: Heidiphyllum denotes Triassic conifer foliage, far younger than this study interval. The clade flags describe that seed-plant affinity; the exceptionally broad collection age does not validate an early occurrence.
source: [Gnaedinger and colleagues, The fossil flora of the Huimpil-Llafquentué Formation, Upper Triassic, Chile](https://revista.macn.gov.ar/index.php/RevMus/article/view/90)

name: Hicklingia edwardi
basis: This denotes Hicklingia edwardii, whose sporangia were reinterpreted as lateral rather than terminal. That morphology supports provisional zosterophyll affinity.
source: [Edwards (1976), The systematic position of Hicklingia edwardii](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10194/)

name: Horneophyton lignieri
basis: A branched sporophyte with columellate sporangia. Reinvestigation identifies conducting cells fundamentally different from tracheids and supports exclusion from Tracheophyta.
source: [Kenrick et al. (2026), Transfer cells in Horneophyton lignieri illuminate the origin of vascular tissues in land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12917476/)

name: Hostinella
basis: A form genus for smooth, usually dichotomising sterile land-plant axes. Anatomy demonstrated in particular species cannot be transferred to every Hostinella identification.
source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from the Lower Old Red Sandstone of south-west Dyfed](https://zenodo.org/records/15904054/files/bhlpart173475.pdf?download=1)

name: Howisonia
basis: Howisonia rara is based on a small sterile stem fragment with apparent filamentous foliage. Superficial lycopod resemblance does not establish a vascular lineage, and the Witpoort provenance needs finer age checking.
source: [Exploring biodiversity patterns among southern African Devonian plants, discussion of Howisonia rara](https://wiredspace.wits.ac.za/server/api/core/bitstreams/0eeb5f47-e296-4067-b3fa-0d43fc9f4306/content)

name: Huia recurvata
basis: Branched axes bear spikes of stalked, recurved lateral sporangia and a centrarch protostele. This unusual combination does not securely resolve lycophyte versus other early vascular-plant affinity.
source: [Geng (1985), Huia recurvata, a new plant from Lower Devonian southeastern Yunnan](https://www.jipb.net/EN/abstract/abstract26233.shtml)

name: Hunanodendrum typicum
basis: Originally described as a graptolite, Hunanodendrum is retained in a modern revision among fossils that cannot currently be assigned to a recognised group. No embryophyte identification is established.
source: [Maletz and Steiner (2021), Treatise Online 152: Uncertain genera](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355267056_Treatise_Online_no_152_Part_V_Second_Revision_Chapter_29_Uncertain_genera)

name: Hyenia
basis: Revised fertile morphology places material called Hyenia elegans with cladoxylopsids, including Calamophyton. Historical uncertainty over generic limits does not alter that broad euphyllophyte affinity.
source: [Fairon-Demaret and Berry (2000), A reconsideration of Hyenia elegans and Hyenia complexa](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10027/)

name: Isidrophyton iniguezii
basis: Repeatedly branching axes terminate in paired, sessile sporangia and show distinctive fusiform surface features. These establish polysporangiate organisation without securely resolving vascular anatomy or crown lineage.
source: [Edwards et al. (2001), Land plants in the Devonian Villavicencio Formation, Mendoza Province, Argentina](https://api.naturalis.fcnym.unlp.edu.ar/server/api/core/bitstreams/9242abeb-8b21-43e9-8183-b6db74f6efb9/content)

name: Jenisseiphyton
basis: Historical descriptions tentatively compare the genus with laminarian algae, whereas later accounts call J. rudnevae lycopod-like. The conflicting interpretations do not support a secure genus-wide assignment.
source: [Osnovy paleontologii (1963), algae and early land plants, p. 191](https://paleosamara.ru/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/osnovy-paleontologii-14-vodorosli-plaunovidnyje.pdf); [Tomsk University account discussing J. rudnevae](https://www.lib.tsu.ru/mminfo/000063105/353/image/353-205.pdf)

name: Jenisseiphyton lebedevii
basis: The historical treatment places this type species tentatively among Laminariales, without demonstrated reproductive organs or a vascular system. Its affinity remains insufficiently resolved.
source: [Osnovy paleontologii (1963), algae and early land plants, p. 191](https://paleosamara.ru/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/osnovy-paleontologii-14-vodorosli-plaunovidnyje.pdf)

name: Jugumella burubaensis
basis: A fertile early land plant compared with zosterophylls, but retained as incertae sedis in the recent comprehensive phylogenetic treatment.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Kidstonophyton discoides
basis: An antheridiophore-bearing gametophyte associated with Nothia aphylla. The flags describe the associated biological lineage, whose crown-tracheophyte placement remains unresolved.
source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Konioria andrychoviensis
basis: Branching axes, reniform sporangia and an exarch conducting strand support its placement among zosterophylls.
source: [Zdebska (1982), A new zosterophyll from the Lower Devonian of Poland, abstract](https://881fe75a-0d59-4523-9a92-1143e3e621d1.eurekamag.com/research/004/603/004603075.php)

name: Krithodeophyton
basis: Branched axes contain protosteles and bear terminal sporangial fructifications. Barinophyte comparisons do not securely resolve its crown lineage.
source: [Edwards (1968), A new plant from the Lower Old Red Sandstone of South Wales](https://palass.org/product/1701); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Langiophyton mackei
basis: This denotes the gametophyte usually spelled Langiophyton mackiei, associated with Horneophyton lignieri. The flags describe that non-tracheophyte polysporangiophyte lineage.
source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/)

name: Leclercqia complexa
basis: A herbaceous lycopsid with vascularised divided leaves, exarch xylem and sporophyll-associated sporangia.
source: [Banks, Bonamo and Grierson (1972), Leclercqia complexa, a new lycopod from eastern New York](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/003466677290005X)

name: Lepidodendropsis
basis: A lycopsid stem genus with a complicated history of species delimitation. Published Lower Devonian attributions exist, so its better-known Carboniferous occurrence does not alone justify exclusion.
source: [Lejal-Nicol and Massa (1980), Lower Devonian plants of Libya, abstract](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/023/619/023619129.php)

name: Leptophloeum australe
basis: An arborescent lycopsid, principally documented from Upper Devonian strata. Its broad PBDB age interval needs checking before interpreting it as an early occurrence.
source: [New Devonian plant fossil occurrences on the New South Wales South Coast: geological implications](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330198067_New_Devonian_plant_fossil_occurrences_on_the_New_South_Wales_South_Coast_geological_implications)

name: Loganiella canadensis
basis: A historical Devonian plant name replacing preoccupied Logania. Its old Psilophytales placement supplies insufficient diagnostic evidence for a modern lineage assignment.
source: [Andrews (1970), Index of generic names of fossil plants, p. 122](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf)

name: Loganophyton
basis: A genuine Devonian plant genus whose relationships remain unresolved. The consulted research abstract treats it among plants that do not fit established categories.
source: [Gensel (2018), The Devonian as a time of major evolutionary innovation and diversification in plants](https://gsa.confex.com/gsa/2018NE/webprogram/Paper310624.html)

name: Lycopodia <sp.>
basis: Interpreted as an informal lycopod group identification. The flags classify the group denoted; neither the spelling nor the underlying occurrence was independently verified.
source: none checked

name: Lycopodia ? sp.
basis: Interpreted as a tentative informal lycopod identification. The flags classify the denoted group, while the occurrence-level identification remains unverified.
source: none checked

name: Lycopodia indet.
basis: Interpreted as an indeterminate lycopod group identification. This does not establish a genus or independently validate the constituent records.
source: none checked

name: Lycopodolica sp.
basis: Compression axes bear hair-like emergences without demonstrated vascular tissue. Published criticism questions their vascular interpretation, preventing a secure lycophyte assignment.
source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

name: Lycopodolica tsegelnjucki n. sp.
basis: The genus has hair-like emergences and possible branching but lacks demonstrated vascular anatomy. A secure polysporangiophyte or lycophyte placement was not established.
source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

name: Lycopodolica tsegelnjuki
basis: Apparently a spelling variant of the preceding Lycopodolica identification. The unresolved nomenclature and absence of demonstrated vascular anatomy preclude secure placement.
source: [Edwards (1979), A late Silurian flora from south-west Dyfed](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_22/vol22_part1_pp23-52.pdf)

name: Lycopsida
basis: A higher-group identification of lycopsids, members of the lycophyte lineage within crown vascular plants.
source: [Xue (2011), Phylogeny of Devonian lycopsids inferred from Bayesian phylogenetic analyses](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1755-6724.2011.00452.x)

name: Lyonophyton rhyniensis n. gen. n. sp.
basis: The gametophyte associated with Aglaophyton. The flags describe its biological lineage, rather than implying that the preserved gametophyte itself bears sporangia.
source: [Taylor et al. (2005), Life history biology of early land plants](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC556298/)

name: Macivera gracilis
basis: A Late Silurian zosterophyll with branching axes and distally dehiscent sporangia clustered near their tips.
source: [Kotyk et al. (2002), Morphologically complex plant macrofossils from the Late Silurian of Arctic Canada](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3732/ajb.89.6.1004)

name: Margophyton
basis: Fertile Siberian Margophyton is a zosterophyll with lateral sporangia. Some European axes historically assigned to it instead represent Psilophyton or remain ambiguous.
source: [Capel et al., Revisiting the Rebreuve plant assemblage from the Lower Devonian of Artois](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302489/1/Revisiting%20the%20Rebreuve%20plant%20assemblage%20from%20the%20Lower%20Devonian%20of%20Artois%20northern%20France.pdf)

name: Mosellophyton hefteri
basis: Originally interpreted as a succulent tracheophyte, these irregularly branching compressions were subsequently combined with Prototaxites. Competing interpretations and inadequate anatomy warrant problematic status.
source: [Palaeoenvironment and palaeoecology of intertidal deposits in a Lower Devonian siliciclastic sequence of the Mosel Region](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233324627_Palaeoenvironment_and_palaeoecology_of_intertidal_deposits_in_a_Lower_Devonian_siliciclastic_sequence_of_the_Mosel_Region_Germany)

name: Nemadophyton dechenianum
basis: Interpreted as the historical Nematophyton dechenianum, with an apparent spelling error. Described tubular tissue lacks a genuine vascular bundle and has unresolved higher affinity.
source: [Historical account of the Elberfeld Middle Devonian flora, Nematophyton dechenianum discussion](https://www.zobodat.at/pdf/Jber-Natwiss-Ver-Elbersfeld_15_0033-0047.pdf)

name: Nematasketum diversiforme
basis: A nematophyte composed of differently sized tubes and hyphae. Anatomical study supports fungal affinity.
source: [Edwards and Axe, Evidence for a fungal affinity for Nematasketum, a close ally of Prototaxites](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/15213/)

name: Nematophyton
basis: The supplied occurrence is Nematophyton taitii, subsequently treated as Prototaxites taiti. Its tubular organisation and disputed higher affinity provide no support for vascular-plant membership.
source: [Honegger et al. (2018), Fertile Prototaxites taiti: a basal ascomycete](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5745340/)

name: Nematoplexus
basis: An enigmatic tubular nematophyte. Plant-like chemical fingerprints do not establish embryophyte identity, sporangial organisation or vascular tissues.
source: [Loron et al. (2023), Molecular fingerprints resolve affinities of Rhynie chert organic fossils](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37047-1)

name: Nematoplexus rhyniensis
basis: A tubular Rhynie nematophyte of debated affinity. Spectroscopic similarity to plant fossilisation products does not demonstrate a polysporangiophyte body plan.
source: [Loron et al. (2023), Molecular fingerprints resolve affinities of Rhynie chert organic fossils](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-37047-1)

name: Nematothallus pseudovasculosa
basis: A nematophyte form taxon with cuticular and tubular components. Reconstructed Nematothallus thalli support fungal or lichen-like rather than embryophyte affinity.
source: [Edwards, Axe and Honegger (2013), Nematothallus revisited](https://doi.org/10.1111/boj.12119)

name: Newspeciesd newspecies
basis: Apparently a database placeholder rather than a recoverable botanical name. The fertile-axis organ label does not establish identity or affinity.
source: none checked

name: Nothia aphylla
basis: A branched sporophyte with numerous lateral sporangia. Conducting-cell and dehiscence differences from typical zosterophylls leave its vascular status and crown placement unresolved.
source: [Edwards (2003), Embryophytic sporophytes in the Rhynie and Windyfield cherts](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/10510/1/Edwards%202003.pdf)

name: Odonax borealis n. sp.
basis: A zosterophyll with branched, spiny axes and strobili of lateral, reniform, bivalved sporangia.
source: [Gerrienne (1996), Lower Devonian plant remains from Marchin: IV. Odonax borealis](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666795001212)

name: Oocampsa catheta
basis: A branched Devonian plant interpreted as intermediate between trimerophytes and progymnosperms. Both alternatives lie on the euphyllophyte lineage.
source: [Wellman and Gensel (2004), Morphology and wall ultrastructure of the spores of Oocampsa catheta, abstract](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/248295329)

name: Oricilla bilinearis n. gen. n. sp.
basis: A zosterophyll with two rows of lateral reniform sporangia on smooth axes, recovered within Sawdoniaceae in recent phylogenetic analysis.
source: [Claisse et al. (2025), Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Pachytheca
basis: Filamentous spheres of conjectural, probably green-algal affinity, without demonstrated embryophyte organisation.
source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

name: Pachytheca ashlayer
basis: Classified by the problematic, probably algal genus Pachytheca. The qualifier ashlayer was not verified as a species name.
source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

name: Pachytheca cf. fasciculata
basis: A qualified Pachytheca identification retains the genus's problematic, probably algal affinity.
source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

name: Pachytheca indet.
basis: Indeterminate Pachytheca represents problematic filamentous spheres, probably green-algal.
source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

name: Pachytheca sp.
basis: Unspecified Pachytheca carries the genus's problematic, probably green-algal affinity.
source: [Edwards et al. (2026), The nature and affinities of Pachytheca](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/187649/)

name: Palaeocancellus
basis: A calcisphere genus including forms interpreted as altered volvocacean algae. Other assigned forms represent different organisms, preventing a uniform algal assignment.
source: [Kaźmierczak (1976), Volvocacean nature of some Palaeozoic non-radiosphaerid calcispheres](https://www.app.pan.pl/archive/published/app21/app21-245.pdf)

name: Palaeogeminella folkii
basis: Originally assigned to green-algal Ulotrichaceae. This remains provisional because filamentous forms from its Caballos Novaculite provenance have also attracted pseudofossil interpretations.
source: [USGS Bulletin 1517, Palaeogeminella entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1517/report.pdf); [Edwards and Lyon (1983), Algae from the Rhynie Chert](https://ir.ucc.edu.gh/xmlui/bitstream/handle/123456789/3757/edwards1983.pdf?sequence=1)

name: Palaeonitella
basis: A charophyte algal genus with anatomically preserved thalli and reproductive structures, outside Embryophyta.
source: [Kelman et al. (2003), Charophyte algae from the Rhynie chert](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0263593300000808)

name: Palaeonitella cranii
basis: An anatomically preserved charophyte with nodal branchlets, antheridia and oogonia.
source: [Kelman et al. (2003), Charophyte algae from the Rhynie chert](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0263593300000808)

name: Palaeostigma
basis: A Devonian axis genus historically compared with lycopsids, but retained incertae sedis in the consulted specimen treatment. Its superficial diagnosis does not securely establish lycophyte or rhyniophyte affinity.
source: [Matsumura and Iannuzzi (2015), Plantas devonianas do Brasil e seu significado bioestratigráfico](https://boletimcn.museu-goeldi.br/bcnaturais/en/article/download/490/235/9974)

name: Palaeostigma sewardi
basis: Incompletely characterised stems belong to a genus historically compared with lycopsids but retained incertae sedis. The PBDB Rhyniaceae placement is insufficiently supported.
source: [Matsumura and Iannuzzi (2015), Plantas devonianas do Brasil e seu significado bioestratigráfico](https://boletimcn.museu-goeldi.br/bcnaturais/en/article/download/490/235/9974)

name: Paleocuticularia perforata n. gen. n. sp.
basis: No diagnostic taxonomic account was recovered. A cuticle occurrence alone cannot establish an embryophyte or vascular-plant parent.
source: none checked

name: Parka
basis: An enigmatic thalloid genus with debated algal and bryophyte comparisons. Its reproductive bodies do not establish a branched polysporangiate sporophyte.
source: [Hemsley (1990), Parka decipiens and land plant spore evolution](https://doi.org/10.1080/08912969009386532)

name: Parka decipiens
basis: A thalloid fossil with alete reproductive bodies compared with algal oospores and bryophyte spores. Its affinity remains enigmatic.
source: [Hemsley (1990), Parka decipiens and land plant spore evolution](https://doi.org/10.1080/08912969009386532)

name: Pathytheca sp.
basis: The exact genus string was not resolved. It may be a transcription of Pachytheca, but the occurrence reference is needed to establish that correction.
source: none checked

name: Pectinophyton
basis: The supplied species P. bipectinatum was transferred to Barinophyton as B. robustius on sporangial architecture. Classification follows that revision and the modern placement of Barinophyton among lycophyte-line barinophytes.
source: [Brauer (1980), Barinophyton citrulliforme, abstract including the transfer of P. bipectinatum](https://documentsdelivered.com/source/001/697/001697241.php); [Claisse et al. (2025)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Perotrilites
basis: A dispersed trilete-spore form genus. Its morphology and PBDB Selaginellaceae hierarchy do not independently establish a lycophyte parent.
source: [Richardson and Lister (1969), Upper Silurian and Lower Devonian spore assemblages from the Welsh Borderland and South Wales](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/palaeontology/volume_12/vol12_part2_pp201-252.pdf)

name: Pertica
basis: A basal euphyllophyte genus with organised lateral branching and terminal sporangial clusters. The supplied P. dalhousii is a recognised trimerophyte.
source: [Doran, Gensel and Andrews (1978), New occurrences of trimerophytes from the Devonian of eastern Canada](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237160469_New_occurrences_of_trimerophytes_from_the_Devonian_of_eastern_Canada)

name: Pertica varia
basis: Explicitly treated as a species of the trimerophyte genus Pertica. Its fertile branching systems and in situ spores support basal euphyllophyte affinity.
source: [Noetinger, Strayer and Tomescu (2018), Spore wall ultrastructure and development in a basal euphyllophyte, comparative discussion](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/ajb2.1137)

name: Pertonella dactylethra n. gen. n. sp.
basis: A late Silurian rhyniophytoid with Cooksonia-like terminal sporangia distinguished by spiny projections. Crown-tracheophyte anatomy is not established.
source: [Fanning, Richardson and Edwards (1991), A review of in situ spores in Silurian land plants](https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780198577461.003.0003)

name: Pinakodendron
basis: The original account assigns the supplied P. corneti from Belgian Early Devonian rocks to a lycopod genus. The sterile material warrants moderate confidence in that attribution.
source: [Ledoux-Marcelle (1930), Sur les flores du Dévonien de la Belgique: II. Pinakodendron corneti](https://biblio.naturalsciences.be/rbins-publications/bulletin-de-la-societe-belge-de-geologie/040%20-%201930/bsbg_040_1930_pv_10-21.pdf)

name: Plantae
basis: A kingdom-level identification cannot establish embryophyte affinity, sporophyte architecture or vascular lineage; the assorted organ descriptions do not resolve this.
source: none checked

name: Praeramunculus
basis: A form genus for branching axes of uncertain affinity. Similarity to Flabellopteris does not establish an organic connection to its diagnostic appendages or justify a progymnosperm assignment.
source: [Gess and Prestianni (2022), Flabellopteris lococannensis gen. et sp. nov.: A new fern-like plant from the Famennian of South Africa](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302493/1/1-s2.0-S0034666721002098-main.pdf)

name: Proteolobus wallii
basis: Described as an acritarch and possible coenobial alga, rather than an embryophyte macrofossil.
source: [Wood (1997), The Acritarch Proteolobus wallii gen. et sp. nov. from the Devonian Iquiri Formation of Bolivia: A Possible Coenobial Alga; publisher contents consulted](https://www.jstor.org/stable/i265474)

name: Protobarinophyton obrutschevii
basis: Protobarinophyton is recovered within lycophytine Barinophytaceae, characterised by specialised fertile systems with lenticular, vertically flattened sporangia.
source: [Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls with a comprehensively sampled dataset and a combination of traditional and new alternative methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Protocephalopteris praecox
basis: A rhacophyte-grade plant with differentiated branching orders and fertile appendages bearing elongate sporangia. Its detailed reconstruction remains questionable because the material is fragmentary.
source: [Gess and Prestianni (2022), Flabellopteris lococannensis gen. et sp. nov.: A new fern-like plant from the Famennian of South Africa](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/302493/1/1-s2.0-S0034666721002098-main.pdf)

name: Protohyenia janovii
basis: Published anatomical reassessment assigns Protohyenia to cladoxylalean plants. Its exclusion from a more narrowly defined Iridopteridales does not exclude it from euphyllophytes.
source: [Flora of the Byskar Series of the Minusinsk Trough and its stratigraphic significance, dissertation summary](https://t.dissercat.com/content/flora-byskarskoi-serii-minusinskogo-progiba-i-ee-stratigraficheskoe-znachenie); [Berry et al. (2022), Ibyka study, taxonomic discussion](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/150085/1/Ibyka%20Berry%20et%20al%202022.pdf)

name: Protolepidodendron
basis: A lycopsid genus traditionally diagnosed by leafy branching axes and forked microphylls. Species circumscription and some historical assignments require revision.
source: [Meyen (1987), Fundamentals of Palaeobotany, discussion of Protolepidodendrales](https://www.ginras.ru/library/pdf/meyen1987.pdf)

name: Protolepidodendropsis
basis: Protolepidodendropsis pulchra is an arborescent lycopsid documented with enlarged stem bases and rooting systems.
source: [Lycopsid forests in the early Late Devonian paleoequatorial zone of Svalbard](https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/gsa/geology/article/43/12/1043/131717/Lycopsid-forests-in-the-early-Late-Devonian?searchresult=1)

name: Protophyllum
basis: Protophyllum Lesquereux is an angiosperm leaf genus documented from Cretaceous deposits, making its literal application to Silurian material implausible. The identity of the extract's P. cylindricum remains unresolved and could reflect a homonym or transcription error.
source: [Krassilov (1973), Cuticular structures of Cretaceous angiosperms, Protophyllum treatment](https://paleobotany.ru/pdf/Krassilov%201973%20-%20Cuticular%20structures%20of%20Cretaceous%20angiosperms.pdf)

name: Protopteridium
basis: Protopteridium has been applied to aneurophyte progymnosperm material also named Milleria or Rellimia. The nomenclature is disputed, but this interpretation places the genus among euphyllophytes.
source: [Matten and Schweitzer (1982), On the correct name for Protopteridium (Rellimia) thomsonii (fossil)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2307/1220002)

name: Protopteridium hostinense
basis: Classified under the interpretation linking Krejčí's Protopteridium material with the Milleria–Rellimia progymnosperm complex. The sterile occurrence alone does not demonstrate the anatomy or fertility underlying that interpretation.
source: [Matten and Schweitzer (1982), On the correct name for Protopteridium (Rellimia) thomsonii (fossil)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2307/1220002)

name: Protosawdonia prima n. gen. n. sp.
basis: A sterile spinous axis compared with Sawdonia and lycopsid-like plants. Without diagnostic fertile structures or vascular anatomy, the resemblance does not establish a lycophyte-line placement.
source: [Cai et al. (1993), New observations on a Pridoli plant assemblage from north Xinjiang, northwest China, with comments on its evolutionary and palaeogeographical significance](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10852/1/Cai%201993.pdf)

name: Prototaxites
basis: A terrestrial organism composed of tubular tissues, without embryophyte sporophyte organisation. Its disputed fungal or extinct-eukaryote affinity does not support inclusion among land plants.
source: [Prototaxites fossils are structurally and chemically distinct from extinct and extant Fungi (2026)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12822639/)

name: Pseudosporochnus
basis: A cladoxylopsid with a complex primary vascular system and digitate branches bearing fertile ultimate appendages.
source: [Berry and Fairon-Demaret (2002), The Architecture of Pseudosporochnus nodosus Leclercq et Banks: A Middle Devonian Cladoxylopsid from Belgium](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/1231/1/Berry%202002.pdf)

name: Psilodendrion spinulosum
basis: Known as a spiny branching plant of uncertain affinity. Sterile external morphology does not establish the Psilophyton-like reproductive organisation needed for a euphyllophyte assignment.
source: [Devonian landscape study of Svalbard, table describing Psilodendrion spinulosum](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/449812/1/Marshall_Devonian_landscape.pdf)

name: Psilophytites
basis: A form genus for sterile psilophyte-like axes with spreading, undivided spines; those characters do not establish a vascular lineage.
source: [Andrews (1970), Index of Generic Names of Fossil Plants, 1820–1965, Psilophytites entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf)

name: Psilophyton
basis: In its revised sense, a trimerophyte-grade euphyllophyte with differentiated branching and terminal sporangial clusters. Historical identifications can include plants subsequently transferred elsewhere.
source: [Banks (1980), The role of Psilophyton in the evolution of vascular plants](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666780900561)

name: Psilophyton dawsonii
basis: A basal euphyllophyte with a centrarch protostele and repeatedly divided fertile branches terminating in paired sporangia.
source: [Spore wall ultrastructure and development in a basal euphyllophyte: Psilophyton dawsonii from the Lower Devonian of Quebec (Canada)](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/ajb2.1137)

name: Psilophyton princeps
basis: Psilophyton sensu stricto belongs to the trimerophyte grade. Older P. princeps identifications require care because the original broad concept combined material subsequently separated into other genera.
source: [Banks (1980), The role of Psilophyton in the evolution of vascular plants](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666780900561)

name: Psilophytopsida
basis: This historical broad grouping combines early branched sporophytes subsequently separated into rhyniophyte, zosterophyll and trimerophyte groups. It cannot be treated as a euphyllophyte identification.
source: [Banks (1975), Reclassification of Psilophyta](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2307/1219491)

name: Rebuchia
basis: The genus is based on a zosterophyll with naked branching axes and lateral sporangia. This generic placement does not validate all referred species, especially poorly preserved R. pendula material.
source: [Hueber (1972), Rebuchia ovata, its vegetative morphology and classification with the Zosterophyllophytina](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666772900127); [Kotyk et al. (2002), Morphologically complex plant macrofossils from the Late Silurian of Arctic Canada](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3732/ajb.89.6.1004)

name: Reimannia
basis: An anatomically preserved Devonian euphyllophyte discussed in relation to progymnosperms. Its historical placement in Iridopteridineae was subsequently rejected.
source: [Berry et al. (2022), Ibyka study, discussion of Reimannia and the circumscription of Iridopteridales](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/150085/1/Ibyka%20Berry%20et%20al%202022.pdf)

name: Renalia
basis: Renalia has branching lateral systems terminated by rounded to reniform sporangia. Terminal attachment resembles rhyniophytoids, whereas distal dehiscence resembles zosterophylls.
source: [Gensel (1976), Renalia hueberi, a new plant from the lower Devonian of Gaspé](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666776900099)

name: Renalia hueberi
basis: Pseudomonopodial axes bear dichotomous laterals ending in reniform sporangia with distal dehiscence. This character combination does not securely establish membership of either crown-tracheophyte lineage.
source: [Gensel (1976), Renalia hueberi, a new plant from the lower Devonian of Gaspé](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666776900099)

name: Retustoriletes raise
basis: The name could not be resolved reliably. It resembles a corrupted spore-morphotaxon name, but neither a spelling correction nor a parent-plant assignment is justified.
source: none checked

name: Rhabdophyton striatus
basis: Described as a leafless Lower Devonian axis of uncertain affinity; diagnostic reproductive structures and lineage-defining anatomy are lacking.
source: [Andrews (1970), Index of Generic Names of Fossil Plants, 1820–1965, Rhabdophyton entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf)

name: Rhachiopteris
basis: The genus was established for a fragment interpreted doubtfully as a fern rachis. An unspecified sterile record cannot establish fern affinity or crown-tracheophyte membership.
source: [Andrews (1970), Index of Generic Names of Fossil Plants, 1820–1965, Rhachiopteris entry](https://pubs.usgs.gov/bul/1300/report.pdf)

name: Rhynia
basis: Rhynia has naked branching sporophytes with terminal sporangia and S-type conducting cells, conventionally placed outside crown tracheophytes. The included Rhynia major is now Aglaophyton and also lies outside that crown.
source: [Cascales-Miñana et al. (2019), An alternative model for the earliest evolution of vascular plants](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/240279/1/Cascales-Minana%20et%20al.%202019_Lethaia.pdf); [Teruelia diezii gen. et sp. nov. (2017), discussion of Aglaophyton](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pala.12277)

name: Rhyniophytina indet.
basis: An explicit rhyniophyte-grade identification supports a simple polysporangiate sporophyte, but the historical subdivision does not by itself establish crown membership.
source: [Banks (1975), Reclassification of Psilophyta](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2307/1219491)

name: Salopella australia
basis: Interpreted as Salopella, probably a spelling error for S. australis. The genus comprises simple branching fertile systems with elongate terminal sporangia and unresolved vascular affinity.
source: [McSweeney et al. (2021), Early land plants from the Lower Devonian of central Victoria, Australia, including a new species of Salopella](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355868791_Early_land_plants_from_the_Lower_Devonian_of_central_Victoria_Australia_including_a_new_species_of_Salopella)

name: Salopella australis
basis: Erect axes dichotomise into branches terminating in elongate sporangia. The external morphology supports rhyniophytoid grade but does not establish crown placement.
source: [McSweeney et al. (2021), Early land plants from the Lower Devonian of central Victoria, Australia, including a new species of Salopella](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355868791_Early_land_plants_from_the_Lower_Devonian_of_central_Victoria_Australia_including_a_new_species_of_Salopella)

name: Salopella brasiliana n. sp.
basis: Classified at genus level as a Salopella-type plant with branching axes and elongate terminal sporangia. The Brazilian species diagnosis was not independently verified.
source: [An early Devonian flora from the Baviaanskloof Formation (Table Mountain Group) of South Africa (2021), comparison of Salopella-type fertile systems](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8178408/)

name: Salopella caespitosa
basis: Repeatedly branching axes terminate in elongate sporangia; the revised material supports a rhyniophytoid organisation without establishing vascular lineage.
source: [McSweeney et al. (2021), Early land plants from the Lower Devonian of central Victoria, Australia, including a new species of Salopella](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/355868791_Early_land_plants_from_the_Lower_Devonian_of_central_Victoria_Australia_including_a_new_species_of_Salopella)

name: Salopella indet.
basis: Salopella-type dichotomous fertile axes bear terminal fusiform sporangia. Generic attribution does not resolve vascular or crown-tracheophyte status.
source: [The southwesternmost record of late Silurian (Pridolian) early land plants of Gondwana (2024)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-63196-4)

name: Salopella marcensis n. sp.
basis: A rhyniophytoid with smooth dichotomising axes and elongate terminal sporangia; crown-defining anatomy is unavailable.
source: [Fanning, Edwards and Richardson (1992), A diverse assemblage of early land plants from the Lower Devonian of the Welsh Borderland](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10174/)

name: Salopella sp.
basis: Generic morphology consists of simple dichotomous fertile axes ending in elongate sporangia; it does not distinguish a crown-tracheophyte lineage.
source: [An early Devonian flora from the Baviaanskloof Formation (Table Mountain Group) of South Africa (2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8178408/)

name: Sawdonia acanthotheca n. sp.
basis: A spinous zosterophyll bearing lateral sporangia, supporting placement on the lycophyte line.
source: [Gensel, Andrews and Forbes (1975), A New Species of Sawdonia with Notes on the Origin of Microphylls and Lateral Sporangia](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/239429119_A_New_Species_of_Sawdonia_with_Notes_on_the_Origin_of_Microphylls_and_Lateral_Sporangia)

name: Sawdonia ornata
basis: The type-locality material establishes Sawdonia as a zosterophyll with spiny axes and lateral sporangia. Some geographically distant referrals remain questionable.
source: [Gensel and Berry (2016), Sporangial Morphology of the Early Devonian Zosterophyll Sawdonia ornata from the Type Locality (Gaspé)](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/687301)

name: Sawdonia sp.
basis: Sawdonia is a zosterophyll genus defined through its spinous axes, vascular anatomy and lateral sporangia; the generic assignment implies lycophyte-line membership.
source: [Hueber (1972), Rebuchia ovata, its vegetative morphology and classification with the Zosterophyllophytina, comparison with Sawdonia](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666772900127)

name: Sawdonia wyomingense n. sp.
basis: Classified as the indicated genus Sawdonia, a lycophytine zosterophyll. The validity and specimen basis of this particular species combination were not independently resolved.
source: [Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls with a comprehensively sampled dataset and a combination of traditional and new alternative methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Sciadophyton
basis: Usually interpreted as an axial gametophyte with terminal gametangiophores, possibly belonging to rhyniophyte-grade plants. Its sporophyte association remains unproved, so neither bryophyte affinity nor crown membership follows.
source: [Gerrienne and Gonez (2011), Early evolution of life cycles in embryophytes: A focus on the fossil evidence of gametophyte–sporophyte size and morphological complexity](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/101745/1/Gerrienne%26Gonez2011.pdf)

name: Selaginellites gracilis
basis: Selaginellites denotes selaginellalean lycophyte material. The equivalence to the extract's Cheirolepis cf. gracilis identification and its Devonian provenance remain unverified.
source: [Seward (1910), Fossil Plants, Volume 2, treatment of Selaginellites and Lycopodites](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/68470/68470-h/68470-h.htm)

name: Serrulacaulis furcatus
basis: A zosterophyll with bifurcate aerial axes, opposite rows of characteristic emergences and lateral sporangia arranged in two rows.
source: [Morphological study on the Devonian zosterophyll Serrulacaulis Hueber and Banks: New materials and emendation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1871174X11000242)

name: Sphondylophyton hyenioides
basis: Reinvestigation rejected the supposed sphenophyte affinity and interpreted its flexuous axes and whorled appendages as a red-algal thallus.
source: [Steenbock and Tomescu (2013), Resurrecting Sphondylophyton as a Rhodophyte Alga from the Early Devonian](https://mihaibotany.online/pdf/SteenbockTomescu2013.pdf)

name: Spongiophyton
basis: A problematic thalloid organism, often interpreted as lichenised, without evidence of embryophyte sporophyte organisation.
source: [The rise of lichens during the colonization of terrestrial environments](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12571074/)

name: Sporangites
basis: The extract specifically identifies S. huronensis, historically mistaken for vascular-plant spores or sporangia but subsequently associated with Tasmanites-type prasinophyte phycomata.
source: [Palynostratigraphie des Pennsylvanium in Deutschland (2005), historical discussion of Sporangites huronensis](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/235986530_Palynostratigraphie_des_Pennsylvanium_in_Deutschland)

name: Sporogonites
basis: Generally interpreted as moss-like material with an unbranched stalk and terminal capsule. Incomplete preservation leaves open whether some specimens are distal fragments of more elaborate sporophytes.
source: [Andrews (1958), Notes On Belgian Specimens of Sporogonites](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.54991/jop.1958.573)

name: Sporogonites exuberans
basis: Unbranched capsule-bearing axes and the lack of demonstrated vascular tissue favour bryophyte affinity. The incompleteness of the plants prevents categorical exclusion of a polysporangiate parent.
source: [Andrews (1958), Notes On Belgian Specimens of Sporogonites](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.54991/jop.1958.573)

name: Stockmansella langii
basis: A rhyniopsid with branching ribbon-like axes, lateral fusiform sporangia and S-type conducting cells, conventionally placed outside crown tracheophytes.
source: [On the origin of euphyllophyte roots: hypotheses from an Early Devonian Psilophyton, comparative table including Stockmansella](https://academic.oup.com/aob/advance-article-pdf/doi/10.1093/aob/mcaf121/63481564/mcaf121.pdf)

name: Stocksmansella langii
basis: Interpreted as the misspelt Stockmansella langii, a rhyniopsid with S-type conducting cells and lateral fusiform sporangia.
source: [On the origin of euphyllophyte roots: hypotheses from an Early Devonian Psilophyton, comparative table including Stockmansella](https://academic.oup.com/aob/advance-article-pdf/doi/10.1093/aob/mcaf121/63481564/mcaf121.pdf)

name: Streptophyta
basis: Streptophyta includes both algae and embryophytes, while the underlying identification Thallophyta indet. is an obsolete broad label. Neither establishes a land-plant lineage.
source: none checked

name: Svalbardia
basis: A progymnosperm-grade genus with differentiated branching and fertile appendages; anatomically associated S. polymorpha material supports archaeopteridalean affinity.
source: [Devonian landscape study of Svalbard, treatment of Svalbardia polymorpha and Actinopodium](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/449812/1/Marshall_Devonian_landscape.pdf)

name: Svalbardia polymorpha
basis: A woody archaeopteridalean progymnosperm with differentiated leafy and fertile branching systems.
source: [Devonian landscape study of Svalbard, Svalbardia polymorpha–Actinopodium association](https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/449812/1/Marshall_Devonian_landscape.pdf)

name: Svalbardia scotica
basis: A Svalbardia-type progymnosperm with differentiated fertile branching, compared directly with S. polymorpha and Archaeopteris.
source: [Allen and Marshall, Devonian Svalbardia and 'corduroy' plant, Special Papers in Palaeontology 35](https://palass.org/sites/default/files/media/publications/special_papers_in_palaeontology/number_35/spp35_pp7-20.pdf)

name: Taeniocrada
basis: A heterogeneous form genus commonly used for sterile ribbon-like axes with a central strand. Anatomically established vascular species cannot justify transferring vascular or crown status to all such fragments.
source: [Taylor (1986), Anatomical and morphological study of a new species of Taeniocrada, a Devonian tracheophyte from New York State](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0034666786900060); [Discovery of a Lochkovian flora in the Iberian Peninsula](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232693054_Discovery_of_a_Lochkovian_flora_Lower_Devonian_in_the_Iberian_Peninsula)

name: Taeniopteris
basis: A leaf morphogenus encompassing fern and seed-plant foliage, with an established Carboniferous–Mesozoic record rather than a Silurian–Middle Devonian one. The extract's extremely broad age interval does not establish an occurrence in the study window.
source: [Journal of Paleontology 90 (2016), Taeniopteris treatment and Carboniferous–Cretaceous range](https://repository.si.edu/bitstreams/7b6373d2-4a0e-46c3-9770-061925608ab3/download)

name: Tarrantia salopensis n. gen. n. sp.
basis: A rhyniophytoid with naked dichotomising axes ending in ovate or elliptical sporangia; anatomy does not establish crown placement.
source: [Fanning, Edwards and Richardson (1992), A diverse assemblage of early land plants from the Lower Devonian of the Welsh Borderland](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10174/)

name: Thamnocladus
basis: Thamnocladus denotes branching thalloid remains generally interpreted as algae; comparable Lower Devonian material has been referred to Buthotrephis. The exact affinity of T. mosellae remains incompletely documented.
source: [Poschmann (2008), Ein außergewöhnlicher Seeskorpion-Fund aus dem Unterdevon des Westerwaldes, associated algal remains](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260115062_Ein_aussergewohnlicher_Seeskorpion-Fund_Chelicerata_Eurypterida_aus_dem_Unterdevon_des_Westerwaldes)

name: Thursophyton milleri
basis: Branching spinous axes contain tracheids, establishing vascular affinity. Lycopsid or zosterophyll relationships are plausible, but the supposed fertile structures remain doubtful.
source: [Perry (1989), The fossil flora of Shetland and surrounding areas](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/files/34493104/DX089503_1.pdf)

name: Tortilicaulis transwalliensis
