basis: Twisted fertile axes and elongate sporangia support rhyniophytoid grade. Recent tracheid evidence concerns T. offaeus and does not settle the precise placement of T. transwalliensis or the genus within stem versus crown tracheophytes.
source: [Lower Devonian Tortilicaulis is an early tracheophyte and not a bryophyte (2024)](https://www.nm.cz/en/periodicals/fossil-imprint-acta-musei-nationalis-pragae-series-b-historia-naturalis/80-1/lower-devonian-tortilicaulis-is-an-early-tracheophyte-and-not-a-bryophyte)

name: Tracheophyta
basis: The identification establishes a vascular plant in PBDB's broad usage. That usage can include early stem tracheophytes and therefore does not independently establish crown membership.
source: [Banks (1975), Reclassification of Psilophyta, historical circumscription of early Tracheophyta](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2307/1219491)

name: Trichopherophyton teuchansii
basis: Exarch xylem and lateral, marginally dehiscent sporangia establish zosterophyll affinity; unicellular spinous hairs distinguish the genus.
source: [Lyon and Edwards (1991), The first zosterophyll from the Lower Devonian Rhynie Chert, Aberdeenshire](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/earth-and-environmental-science-transactions-of-royal-society-of-edinburgh/article/abs/first-zosterophyll-from-the-lower-devonian-rhynie-chert-aberdeenshire/FE5618260705743ECCEA0341737C9C5B)

name: Trimerophyton
basis: The defining trimerophyte genus has differentiated branching systems bearing numerous terminal sporangia; trimerophytes are basal euphyllophytes.
source: [Hopping (1956), On a Specimen of Psilophyton robustius Dawson, from the Lower Devonian of Canada](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-royal-society-of-edinburgh-section-b-biological-sciences/article/abs/iion-a-specimen-of-psilophyton-robustius-dawson-from-the-lower-devonian-of-canada/A3501A4C4069252E6BB5052E7ED9B690); [Psilophyton spore study, comparison with basal euphyllophyte Trimerophyton](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/ajb2.1137)

name: Trochiliscus
basis: A charophyte genus identified from reproductive utricles with numerous dextrally spiralled cells; these are algal reproductive structures.
source: [Treatise on Invertebrate Paleontology, Charophyta, Trochiliscus treatment](https://charophyte.treatise.geolex.org/displayInfo.php?genera=Trochiliscus)

name: Uralia
basis: Uralia camdjalensis is retained as a satellite form taxon among Devonian pteridophyte material. The consulted treatment does not establish a particular vascular lineage.
source: [Phytostratigraphy of the Devonian of southeastern Gorny Altai, systematic list including Uralia](https://www.earthpapers.net/fitostratigrafiya-devona-yugo-vostoka-gornogo-altaya)

name: Urpicalis steemansii
basis: Isotomously branched fertile systems bear elongate sporangia along their adaxial surfaces and sometimes at dichotomies. Proposed progymnosperm relationships remain insufficiently demonstrated.
source: [Hao, Gensel and Wang (2001), Polythecophyton demissum, gen. et sp. nov., a new plant from the Lower Devonian of Yunnan, comparison with Urpicalis](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240390384_Polythecophyton_demissum_gen_et_sp_nov_a_new_plant_from_the_Lower_Devonian_Pragian_of_Yunnan_China_and_its_phytogeographic_significance)

name: Uskiella reticulata n. sp.
basis: A rhyniophytoid with branching naked axes terminating in elongate sporangia; the preserved characters do not establish a crown lineage.
source: [Fanning, Edwards and Richardson (1992), A diverse assemblage of early land plants from the Lower Devonian of the Welsh Borderland](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10174/)

name: Wattieza
basis: A cladoxylopsid with digitate branching and repeatedly bifurcating fertile appendages bearing terminal sporangia.
source: [Berry (2000), A reconsideration of Wattieza Stockmans, here attributed to Cladoxylopsida, based on a new species from the Devonian of Venezuela](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11042329/)

name: Yarravia
basis: Revised material unites Yarravia and Hedeia preservational forms as branching fructifications with terminal sporangia. Rhyniophytoid affinity is favoured, while vascular and euphyllophyte placement remain unproved.
source: [McSweeney et al. (2021), Yarravia oblonga Lang & Cookson, 1935 emended, from the Lower Devonian of Victoria, Australia](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354148905_Yarravia_oblonga_Lang_Cookson_1935_emended_from_the_Lower_Devonian_of_Victoria_Australia)

name: Yarravia oblonga
basis: The supposed synangium was reinterpreted as a preservation artefact of a branching fertile system. Its organisation supports rhyniophytoid grade without demonstrating crown-tracheophyte membership.
source: [McSweeney et al. (2021), Yarravia oblonga Lang & Cookson, 1935 emended, from the Lower Devonian of Victoria, Australia](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354148905_Yarravia_oblonga_Lang_Cookson_1935_emended_from_the_Lower_Devonian_of_Victoria_Australia)

name: Zosterophyllales
basis: An explicit zosterophyll identification places the material on the lycophyte line, characterised by lateral sporangia and generally exarch vascular systems.
source: [Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls with a comprehensively sampled dataset and a combination of traditional and new alternative methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: Zosterophyllum
basis: A lycophyte-line genus of branching vascular plants bearing lateral sporangia, commonly concentrated in spikes.
source: [Uncoupling of morphological disparity and species diversity in Zosterophyllum, with its new species from the Pridoli of West Junggar, Xinjiang, China](https://academic.oup.com/aob/article/137/6/1646/8405492)

name: Zosterophyllum divaricatum
basis: Branching fertile axes carry lateral sporangia oriented towards one side, with vascular anatomy supporting zosterophyll affinity.
source: [Gensel (1982), A New Species of Zosterophyllum from the Early Devonian of New Brunswick](https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1002/j.1537-2197.1982.tb13305.x)

name: Zosterophyllum myretonianum
basis: The type species of Zosterophyllum bears lateral sporangia assembled into fertile spikes; detailed sporangial and stalk morphology supports its zosterophyll identification.
source: [Edwards (1975), Some Observations on the Fertile Parts of Zosterophyllum myretonianum Penhallow from the Lower Old Red Sandstone of Scotland](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259412832_11-Some_Observations_on_the_Fertile_Parts_of_Zosterophyllum_myretonianum_Penhallow_from_the_Lower_Old_Red_Sandstone_of_Scotland)

name: cf. Salopella sp.
basis: Classified as the indicated Salopella-type genus, with dichotomous fertile axes and terminal fusiform sporangia. The comparison qualifier preserves uncertainty in the specimen identification.
source: [The southwesternmost record of late Silurian (Pridolian) early land plants of Gondwana (2024)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-63196-4)

name: cf. Sawdonia ornata
basis: The indicated genus is a spinous zosterophyll. The sterile comparison identification does not independently verify the diagnostic sporangial characters of S. ornata.
source: [Gensel and Berry (2016), Sporangial Morphology of the Early Devonian Zosterophyll Sawdonia ornata from the Type Locality (Gaspé)](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/687301)

name: cf. Sawdonia sp.
basis: Classified as the indicated zosterophyll genus Sawdonia. The comparison qualifier concerns identification of the occurrence, rather than the established lineage of the genus.
source: [Re-evaluating the phylogenetic relationships of zosterophylls with a comprehensively sampled dataset and a combination of traditional and new alternative methods](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13274996/)

name: cf. Tortilicaulis sp.
basis: Classified as Tortilicaulis, a genus including branching sporophytes with elongate sporangia and demonstrated tracheids. Its position within stem or crown tracheophytes remains unresolved.
source: [Lower Devonian Tortilicaulis is an early tracheophyte and not a bryophyte (2024)](https://www.nm.cz/en/periodicals/fossil-imprint-acta-musei-nationalis-pragae-series-b-historia-naturalis/80-1/lower-devonian-tortilicaulis-is-an-early-tracheophyte-and-not-a-bryophyte)

name: cf. Uskiella reticulata
basis: Classified as the indicated rhyniophytoid genus Uskiella, with branching fertile axes and terminal elongate sporangia. Neither the comparison identification nor generic morphology establishes crown placement.
source: [Fanning, Edwards and Richardson (1992), A diverse assemblage of early land plants from the Lower Devonian of the Welsh Borderland](https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/10174/)
